New research points to the role of circadian rhythms in depression.
The study from a team at the University of Sydney suggests that as many as
one in four people with that diagnosis could have a distinct type of depression

The study used a database of about 10,000 adults in Australia with depression.
The researchers came up with different criteria. They looked at sleep schedule,

Based on that, they found just under 25 percent of adults fit this profile for circadian depression.
A key finding was that they tended to have less success with SSRIs, the most commonly prescribed

emphasized the study is a proof of concept and needs to be replicated in other populations,
